reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is that RLHF's distortion arises from mismatches between the preference data-generating distribution μ and the reference policy π_ref. This leads to an exponential scaling of distortion with β, unless B = 0 (i.e., perfect alignment). The key innovation lies in refining this bound using reward clipping and introducing the concept of effective utility, which isolates the portion of utility preserved in pairwise comparisons. The distortion bound is expressed as a function of B, τ, and β, where B quantifies the maximum deviation of log(π_ref/μ), τ bounds KL divergence, and β controls the sensitivity of Bradley-Terry preferences. In GSI context, this translates into Bayesian calibration of user utility models under uncertain feedback, while in GSE, it informs policy selection under bounded information constraints. The failure mode occurs when B is large or τ insufficient, leading to suboptimal alignment.
